question_text: A particle is performing uniform circular motion of radius $3\text{ m}$ with an angular velocity $2\text{ rad/s}$ in clockwise direction as shown. Find acceleration of particle at point $Q$.
diagram_description: A circle in the Cartesian coordinate plane centered at the origin. Point Q is located on the circumference in the first quadrant, with its position vector making an angle of 60° with the positive x-axis. The particle moves in a clockwise direction with radius R = 3 m and angular velocity ω = 2 rad/s.
solution:
In uniform circular motion, the particle has only centripetal acceleration directed radially inward toward the center (the origin).

The magnitude of the centripetal acceleration is:
$$a_c = \omega^2 R = (2\text{ rad/s})^2 \times 3\text{ m} = 12\text{ m/s}^2$$

The position vector of point $Q$ which makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the $+x$-axis is:
$$\hat{r} = \cos 60^\circ\hat{i} + \sin 60^\circ\hat{j} = \frac{1}{2}\hat{i} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{j}$$

Since centripetal acceleration is directed toward the origin (opposite to $\hat{r}$):
$$\vec{a}_c = -a_c \hat{r} = -12\left(\frac{1}{2}\hat{i} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{j}\right) = (-6\hat{i} - 6\sqrt{3}\hat{j})\text{ m/s}^2$$

Therefore, the correct option is (1).

question_text: Find magnitude of average acceleration between the points $P$ and $Q$ for a particle performing uniform circular motion. Radius of circle is $2\text{ m}$.
diagram_description: A circular path with radius R = 2 m. Point P is on the horizontal axis with velocity 4 m/s directed upwards. Point Q is located along the circle such that the angle subtended at the center by arc PQ is 60°, and the velocity at Q has a magnitude of 4 m/s tangent to the circle.
solution:
The magnitude of the change in velocity for a particle moving at constant speed $v$ turning through an angle $\theta$ is:
$$|\Delta \vec{v}| = 2v \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$$
Given $v = 4\text{ m/s}$ and $\theta = 60^\circ$:
$$|\Delta \vec{v}| = 2(4) \sin(30^\circ) = 8 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4\text{ m/s}$$

The time taken $\Delta t$ to travel along the arc from $P$ to $Q$ is:
$$\Delta t = \frac{s}{v} = \frac{R\theta}{v} = \frac{2 \times \frac{\pi}{3}}{4} = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ s}$$

The magnitude of the average acceleration is:
$$a_{\text{avg}} = \frac{|\Delta \vec{v}|}{\Delta t} = \frac{4}{\frac{\pi}{6}} = \frac{24}{\pi}\text{ m/s}^2$$

Taking $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$:
$$a_{\text{avg}} = \frac{24 \times 7}{22} = \frac{168}{22} = \frac{84}{11}\text{ m/s}^2$$

Therefore, the correct option is (1).

question_text: A man can swim at a speed of $5\text{ km/h}$ w.r.t. water. He wants to cross a $1.5\text{ km}$ wide river flowing at $3\text{ km/h}$. He always keeps himself at an angle of $60^\circ$ with the flow direction while swimming. The time taken by him to cross the river will be
solution:
Let the river flow along the positive $x$-direction with speed $v_r = 3\text{ km/h}$.
The width of the river along the $y$-direction is $d = 1.5\text{ km}$.

The swimmer moves at speed $v_{m/w} = 5\text{ km/h}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ with the river flow direction.
The component of his velocity perpendicular to the river flow (responsible for crossing the river) is:
$$v_y = v_{m/w} \sin 60^\circ = 5 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2.5\sqrt{3}\text{ km/h}$$

The time taken to cross the river is:
$$t = \frac{d}{v_y} = \frac{1.5}{2.5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3}{5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\text{ h}$$

Using $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$:
$$t \approx \frac{1.732}{5} \approx 0.3464\text{ h} \approx 0.35\text{ h}$$

Therefore, the correct option is (2).

question_text: Two particles 1 and 2 are allowed to descend on the two frictionless chords $OA$ and $OB$ of vertical circle at the same instant from point $O$. The ratio of the velocities of the particles 1 and 2, when they reach the circumference will be ($OB$ is diameter)
diagram_description: A vertical circle with top-most point O. Chord OB represents the vertical diameter of length D. Chord OA is inclined at an angle α with the vertical diameter OB. Particles 1 and 2 descend from O along OA and OB, respectively.
solution:
Let the vertical diameter $OB = D$.

For particle 2 descending along the vertical diameter $OB$:
- Distance $s_2 = D$
- Acceleration $a_2 = g$
- Velocity at $B$:
$$v_2 = \sqrt{2 a_2 s_2} = \sqrt{2 g D}$$

For particle 1 descending along chord $OA$ inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the vertical diameter $OB$:
- Since $\angle OAB = 90^\circ$ (angle inscribed in a semicircle), the length of chord $OA$ is:
$$s_1 = D \cos\alpha$$
- The acceleration along the chord $OA$ is the component of gravity along $OA$:
$$a_1 = g \cos\alpha$$
- Velocity at $A$:
$$v_1 = \sqrt{2 a_1 s_1} = \sqrt{2 (g \cos\alpha)(D \cos\alpha)} = \sqrt{2 g D \cos^2\alpha} = \sqrt{2 g D} \cos\alpha$$

Taking the ratio of their velocities:
$$\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{\sqrt{2 g D}\cos\alpha}{\sqrt{2 g D}} = \cos\alpha$$
Thus, the ratio is $\cos\alpha : 1$.

Therefore, the correct option is (1).
